svg.title: Cultivating a Luminous Mind: Mindfulness & Alertness

g.text: Cultivating a Luminous Mind: Mindfulness & Alertness
Initial State of Mind
Mind is Luminous
Mind is undeveloped, unpliant, leads to great harm
Mind is untamed, unguarded, unprotected, unrestrained
Mind is sullied
- Prevents knowing own/others' benefit and realizing superior human state --
Mind is developed, pliant, leads to great benefit
Mind is tamed, guarded, protected, restrained
Mind is freed from incoming defilements
Cultivation of Mindfulness & Alertness
Discern the luminous mind defiled by incoming defilements
The Dhamma is for one whose
mindfulness is established, not confused.
Recognize oneself as a "well-instructed disciple of the noble ones"
Heedfulness is a bright quality that guards the world, along with compunction.
It is also knowing/knowledge.
Heedlessness is a defilement of the mind.
Practice Heedfulness
Guard mind from passion, aversion, delusion, intoxication
Practice Mindfulness of In-&-Out Breathing
Breathe in/out long or short
Breathe in/out sensitive to entire body
Breathe in/out calming bodily fabrication
Develop it acutely for ending effluents
Practice mindful & astute concentration
Know feelings, perceptions, thoughts as they arise, persist, subside (Nanda's practice)
Remain focused on Body, Feelings, Mind, Mental Qualities in & of themselves
- Be ardent, alert, & mindful, subduing greed & distress --
This develops restraint over senses;
eye does not pull toward pleasing forms.
Practice Mindfulness immersed in the body
Essential for perfect & pure holy life,
along with moderation in eating and wakefulness.
Guard the doors of senses with mindfulness as protector/chief
Be always mindful as one goes forward/back, stands, sits, sleeps, determines action
Make oneself alert in all actions (looking, bending, carrying, eating, talking, etc.)
Develop concentration through mindfulness of in-&-out breathing
- Leads to peaceful & exquisite abiding --
- Immediately disperses & allays evil, unskillful mental qualities --
Develop mindfulness as a factor for awakening
- Dependent on seclusion, dispassion, cessation, resulting in letting go --
- Discern mind is released, sloth/drowsiness uprooted, restlessness/anxiety subdued, persistence aroused, attention focused --
Desired Outcomes
Mind is pliant, malleable, luminous, not brittle
Mind is rightly concentrated for the ending of effluents
Achieve Purity of Mind
Realize a superior human state, noble distinction of knowledge & vision
Attain "Unprovoked (release)"
End the effluents
Mind is released from effluents through lack of clinging
Overcome sorrow & lamentation, disappear pain & distress
Attain the right method and realize unbinding
Achieve gnosis right in the here-&-now, or non-return
Mindfulness serves every purpose
Pains arising in body do not invade or remain in the mind
Hindrances and Lack of Practice
Dwelling in Heedlessness
- Mind is stained with forms cognizable via the eye (if no restraint);
- No joy, rapture, calm --
- Dwells in pain, mind unconcentrated --
- Phenomena don't become manifest --
- Reckoned simply as one who dwells in heedlessness --
Mindfulness is confused
Lack of guarding the doors of senses
Not devoted to wakefulness
Not endowed with mindfulness & alertness
Experiencing doubt, inattention, sloth-&-drowsiness, panic, excitement, boredom, excess/slack persistence, perception of multiplicity, excessive absorption in forms
- These defilements cause concentration to fall away and light/forms to disappear --
